findings.finding: The FY27 guide, due at this print, is set into what NOAA's sources call a possibly record El Nino. drought.gov's November 2026 Great Lakes ENSO brief gives an 83% chance this is the strongest El Nino since 1950. NOAA CPC's Nov 19 update favors above-normal Dec-Feb temperatures across much of the Great Lakes, and NWS Gaylord says trends favor below-normal snowfall, especially lake-effect. That is CMP's core highway-salt footprint, served from Goderich. Management already said in August it will commit to a reduced FY27 volume profile assuming normal winter. A visibly warm early season raises the odds of a conservative volume guide or below-consensus FY27 EBITDA (consensus FY27 EPS $1.26, +40% YoY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last first-guide print (2025-12-08, FY26 guide $200-240M) moved -13.81%. The Q3 print (2026-08-05), which cut the top of the Salt guide and flagged Goderich costs, moved -14.55%. This name sells guide-heavy prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is -10% in 20 days and -7.8% in 5 days, below the post-Q3 low, and the Nov 15 preview did not mention weather. Had the market fully priced a materially lower FY27 volume guide, FY27 consensus EPS would not still sit at +40% YoY. The company's guide convention (a normal-winter assumption) also means the release may not reflect El Nino at all, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro to company, not confirmed by the company. Second source pointing the same way: NWS Gaylord winter outlook https://www.weather.gov/media/apx/WinterOutlook.pdf (below-normal snowfall favored). Also a US Harbors piece, Oct 2026: https://www.usharbors.com/2026/10/el-nino-looms-large-over-u-s-winter-outlook/

findings.finding: Highway deicing pricing for 2026-27 is up roughly double digits overall, and in core US markets 'in some cases well into the double digits' (CEO, Q3 call, 2026-08-06), on 'historically low inventories across the system'. A third-party read of published tenders puts the rise at more than 60% where comparisons exist. This supports FY27 per-ton margin in the guide against lower committed tons.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This was disclosed at the Q3 print (2026-08-05), and the stock fell 14.55% anyway on Salt costs. Pricing news alone has not bought this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it has been public since August. The unpriced part is how much of it reaches the FY27 EBITDA guide after lower tons and Goderich costs. If the market fully credited double-digit price on low inventories, the stock would not be 40% off its high.
findings.independence: Crux Investor tender summary (secondary): https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/road-salt-bids-rise-over-60-why-the-market-still-needs-new-mines . Counter-sample: the DuPage County renewal was only +5% ($70.79 to $74.33/ton), https://agendadocs.downers.us/public/docs/agendas/2026/08_04_2026/MOT_2026-11295.pdf

findings.finding: Goderich operating costs remain the unresolved drag. On the Q3 call management said 'we're not hoisting enough tons out of Goderich at the cost we had planned', plus higher maintenance at both US mines and added headcount. Salt segment EBITDA fell 15% YoY in Q3, the FY26 Salt guide top end was cut from $240M to $236M, and the COO departed and was replaced internally (Brandon Reisner). FY27 cost per ton is the swing factor against the price gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line drove the -14.55% reaction to Q3 on 2026-08-05.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the August drop and a further ~20% slide since. What is not priced is whether the FY27 cost-per-ton assumption shows improvement. With no interim update since August, the first read is this release.
findings.independence: Shares the Q3 release and call with the pricing finding, but a different line (cost, not price). Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-15 frames the print the same way: https://finviz.com/news/422870/compass-minerals-heads-into-fiscal-year-end-needing-proof-that-salt-pricing-can-outrun-goderich-costs

findings.finding: The 50% ad valorem Section 338 tariff applied to Canadian salt from about 2026-08-19 until the exclusion effective 2026-09-15. That window falls entirely inside fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep) and the pre-season fill shipments from Goderich into the US. Gross exposure is mitigated by contract pass-through clauses, and no dollar figure was disclosed. The exclusion removes the risk for FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior tariff-cost print on this name. The exclusion release (2026-09-10) came before the stock slid further.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 cost was never quantified. If it were priced, Q4 consensus would show a visible Salt margin cut, and the -$0.01 EPS consensus is already near breakeven. It is a one-off with no path to the FY27 guide, so it is sized at a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.
findings.independence: Q3 call: pass-through provisions 'reduce exposure meaningfully' (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMP/Q32026). Kansas senator's warning on tariffs: https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2026-08-24/us-sen-jerry-moran-warns-of-canadian-salt-tariffs-effect-on-kansas-taxpayers

findings.finding: Management promised a capital-allocation update 'when we report full-year results'. Net leverage is down to 2.8x from 4.3x, the $150M 2027 notes were redeemed, S&P upgraded the company to B+, and liquidity is $328M. A first shareholder-return step (dividend reinstatement or buyback) is possible at this print, though stated near-term priorities remain asset investment and debt reduction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return announcement on this name in the 7-print baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The content is unknown. A stock below its post-Q3 low on a deleveraged balance sheet does not look priced for a return of capital. Management's stated priority (debt reduction and assets) makes a disappointing 'no return' just as plausible, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Q3 8-K balance-sheet figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227654/000122765426000050/cmp-q32026earningsreleasee.htm (same company source family).

findings.finding: Governance churn after year-end. Director David Safran resigned on 2026-10-09 and the board shrank to eight (8-K filed 2026-10-15). Chief Accounting Officer Ashley Ward resigned on 2026-10-22, effective the next day, three weeks after the 9/30 fiscal year-end and mid-audit. The 8-K says 'not the result of any disagreement'. She was replaced by Brett Teuscher, internal-audit senior director since May 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: These are quiet 8-Ks with no press coverage, absent from the Nov 15 preview. Against an accounting problem: the release comes on schedule and earlier than last year (Nov 23 vs Dec 8, 2025), so this is sized small.

findings.finding: The Q4 FY26 print is effectively pre-set by the guide: midpoint $230M less YTD $191.6M gives $38.4M of Q4 adj. EBITDA (range $26.4-50.4M) vs $41.6M a year ago. Plant Nutrition has beaten its targets four quarters running and was raised to $49-57M. Revenue consensus of $1.28B for FY26 sits slightly above the guide midpoint. A modest Plant Nutrition-led beat inside the range is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats have not protected this stock: Q4 FY25 beat revenue by about $3.8M and the stock moved -13.81% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance, so it is mostly priced and sized near zero.
